title: Why do we get goosebumps?
examples: Teacher, why do I get goosebumps when it gets cold?
What are those little bumps on my skin?
Does getting goosebumps mean I am cold?

explain.say: When you feel cold, your body does something special.

items: Body tries to keep you warm

explain.say: Little tiny muscles near your skin pull your hairs up.

draw.text: Muscles pull hairs up when cold

explain.say: Pulling the hairs up makes you look bigger to animals.
This action helps trap a layer of warm air around you.

draw.text: Traps warm air to stay cozy

explain.say: When you swim in cold water, you might see this happen.
Sometimes, even when you are not cold, you can get them.

items: Seeing something surprising can trigger it

faq.q: Why do I get goosebumps when I am scared?
faq.a: It is because your body thinks it needs to get warmer quickly. It is a leftover trick from when we were much smaller.
asks: Is it always about being cold?

faq.q: Do I still get goosebumps if I have very short hair?
faq.a: Yes, the muscles still try to pull the hairs up, even if the hairs are very short. The feeling is what matters most.
asks: Can I still get them without hair?

faq.q: Are goosebumps a sign that I am sick?
faq.a: No, they are just a normal way your body tries to keep you warm. They do not mean you are getting sick.

faq.q: What are those tiny muscles called?
faq.a: These muscles are called arrector pili muscles. They are very small muscles attached to your hair roots.

faq.q: Is this happening in all animals?
faq.a: Many animals do this too. It is a survival trick that helps them keep warm in the wild.
asks: Is this natural for all creatures?

facts: Goosebumps happen because tiny muscles pull hairs up.
This action helps trap a layer of warm air near the skin.
The body uses this trick to help keep you warm.
It can happen when you are cold, or when you feel excited.

quiz.say: What do the tiny muscles pull up when you feel cold?
quiz.why: The muscles are attached to the hair roots, so they pull the hairs up.

wrong.0: Fat is under the skin, but the muscles pull the hair.
wrong.2: The muscles pull the hairs, not the skin itself.
wrong.3: Blood is for carrying warmth, not for being pulled up by muscles.

quiz.say: If you are cold, what is the main job of the goosebumps?
quiz.why: By making the hairs stand up, the body traps air to keep heat in.

wrong.0: The goal is warmth, not making the skin feel itchy.
wrong.2: While looking bigger is part of it, trapping air is the main goal.
wrong.3: This is an old idea, but trapping air is the real purpose now.

options.show: Only when it is very cold
options.say: Only when it is very cold

quiz.why: Your body reacts to both cold temperatures and sudden strong feelings.

wrong.0: While fear causes it, excitement also causes this reaction.
wrong.1: It can happen in dry air if you are very excited.
wrong.3: You can get them from excitement too, not just cold.
